requirements.title: A program unit uses one source form
requirements.source: 6.3.1 p3, fourth sentence; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF page 71, printed page 57, lines 8-9.
requirements.definition: An individual program unit cannot switch between free-form and fixed-form conventions. This restriction is per program unit, not per complete program. The processor selects how a unit's source form is specified; neither a filename suffix nor a command-line spelling is standardized.
requirements.oracle: The source_forms_separate_units manifest explicitly selects free and fixed form for different compilation inputs, then links and runs them together. The free input contains a main program and a following external subroutine; another external subroutine is fixed form. Calls must produce 37 and then 43. These are positive controls, including uncredited INCLUDE and comment context. The mixed-continuation negative has unmistakably free-form lines starting in column one but imports a fixed-form column-six continuation after a complete, uncontinued assignment. Require a diagnostic on the imported continuation line. Its positive control adds just the missing trailing free-form ampersand to the preceding line and checks the result 3.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This is one concrete mixed-convention witness, not detection of every possible mixture or a processor-independent way to request an in-unit mode switch. Text that happens to be legal in both forms is not a violation. The diagnostic is also explained by 6.3.2.4; that later section is necessary, uncredited context, not a newly authored continuation requirement. The standard requires reporting capability under 4.2 p2(5), not necessarily rejection. The existing runner checks located errors and supported reference-warning classes; unsupported nonfatal reporting paths must not be mistaken for absence of a diagnostic. No exhaustive comment-character, INCLUDE, END, or compiler-selection semantics are claimed.
requirements.dependencies: 4.2 p2(1)/(5), PDF 46, supplies conforming execution and Clause 6 diagnostic obligations. 5.2.1 and 14.1/15.6.2.3 define the program units used here. 6.3.2.1, 6.3.2.4 p1-p2, and 6.3.3.1/6.3.3.3 supply the contrasting layout contexts. Fixed input uses exactly 72 default-kind ASCII characters per line without a continuation case. 6.4 p3-p5, PDF 73, keeps INCLUDE separate from statements. 3.21, PDF 21, defines character contexts; 6.1.1, 6.1.6, and 7.4.4.2 retain character-set ownership.

accounting.rationale: PDF 71, printed 57, lines 3-5: four definitional sentences are accounted separately; they are not four invented runtime requirements.

A program unit is organized from lines containing statements, comments, and INCLUDE lines. The separate-units fixture supplies finite context, not a new S obligation or complete unit grammar coverage.
A line is a possibly empty character sequence. Newline bytes delimit the raw fixture's physical lines and are not counted as source characters.
Source after a program-unit END is outside that unit. A following external subroutine is context in source_forms_separate_units; canonical END and program-unit grammars remain in Clause 14 and 15.
Statements can occupy complete or partial lines. Continuation and termination are defined in later source-form subclauses; no later-section obligation is allocated here.
PDF 71, line 6: comment-character permission is decomposed by the two character contexts in 3.21, not promoted to an all-character compiler test.

Characters admissible in a character literal may occur in a comment. The processor's representable repertoire, including supported additional characters, is not a universal ASCII-only whitelist. The short ASCII comment in the raw control is context only; exhaustive repertoire evidence is source-only.

The same permission includes characters admissible in a character string edit descriptor. This is the second 3.21 context, not a separate mandatory diagnostic or an assertion that comment punctuation is executable syntax.
PDF 71, lines 7-9: distinguish the two forms, their applicability, the intra-unit restriction, and processor-supplied selection.
Identifies free and fixed form. It does not specify file extensions or introduce a third mixed form.
6.3.2 governs the free-form selection, not every source input regardless of processor mode.
6.3.3 governs the fixed-form selection. Its defining catalogues and existing fixed-form calibration remain untouched.
The selection mechanism is processor dependent. Manifest form fields exercise the existing compiler adapters; source filename suffixes are not credited as standard requirements.

review_rationale: Independent source-first review and recorded integration repairs: doc/source_audits/lexical_batch_004.json. Composition definitions, both character contexts, both forms, separate applicability, per-unit nonmixing and processor selection are accounted for. Explicit form flags, not filename suffix semantics, select the two forms. The mixed-continuation negative has the one-ampersand repair.
